$comment: Glass-only elements (Liquid Glass plan 4.4, 8.5; plans/REVISION-DEFAULT.md R13). The 8.5 action-inventory check (stage 4) fails on any glass-only action not listed here. A 'duplicate action' entry names the classic element it duplicates on the same route, behind the same gate; an 'appearance control (no data action)' entry has no classic twin: it changes only the viewer's own appearance and reads or writes no other data; a 'renamed action' entry is a classic element that glass names differently (DECISIONS.md F6). appearance-render.guard.test.ts checks that every data-glass-only element in the source is listed; appearance-select.test.tsx checks the header menu's renamed trigger.

kinds.duplicate action: Goes where an existing classic element on the same route goes, behind the same permission gate; classicTwin names that element.
kinds.appearance control (no data action): The header appearance menu (Design and Theme). No classic twin on the route; no permission gate; touches only the viewer's own appearance (device record, Design cookie, own user_appearance row).
kinds.renamed action: The classic element itself, with the same role, target, position and permission gate, under another accessible name (and tooltip) while <html> carries data-appearance="liquid-glass". name is its glass name and classicTwin its classic name: the 8.5 check counts the two as one action, so walkers find it by either name and the classic name missing in glass is not a missing action.

entries.$comment: ExternalAppearanceCorner. ExternalShell draws it in its page frame when the page passes no top bar; app/r/layout.tsx draws it for /r/[token], /r/track and /r/confirm, whose columns use frame="column" inside that layout. /invite/[token] and /onboarding pass a top bar that already holds the menu. Its trigger is the header menu's, so in glass it is named "Appearance: design and theme" (entry header-appearance-menu-trigger).

entries.name: Appearance: design and theme
entries.$comment: DECISIONS.md F6: the header appearance menu's trigger (ThemeToggle) opens the Design and the Theme, so while <html> shows Liquid Glass it is named, and titled, for both; in Classic, in every rollout, it is origin/main's "Toggle theme" with no tooltip. The routes are those whose classic page shows it: the marketing header (/, the 6 marketing pages), the sign-in layout, the invite and onboarding top bars, and the dashboard top bar on /dashboard and every route under it (/dashboard/**), where it is shown from a 680 px wide bar. On the /dashboard/orders/[id]/print route <html> is never glass, so it keeps its classic name there. The 8 external routes are entry external-appearance-menu: there it exists only in glass.
